tier: US static residential VPS (AT&T line and Verizon line)

free_tier.stated: No free tier. The product page lists a dedicated static AT&T (AS7018) line and a dedicated static Verizon (AS5650) line, each with 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 25 GB SSD, 100 Mbps peak and 2000 GB of two-way traffic, in 'California, multiple cities and segments at random'. A third-party review reports the price as CNY 149 per month for both lines, both showing sold out with a pre-order queue.
free_tier.notes: The price is reported by a third-party review and was not in the first-party page text that could be read.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic quota, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a proxy session or a rented address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: 2000 GB of two-way traffic per month and 100 Mbps peak, both configurable at extra cost; overage behaviour is unstated.

interface_detail: A rented VPS with a dedicated static IPv4 address; the buyer runs any proxy daemon on it. The vendor sells the address and the machine, not a proxy endpoint.
tooling: An SSH client plus a proxy daemon that the user installs and runs on the VPS (a rented machine, not owned hardware). The vendor publishes no proxy endpoint or API for the static line.
chaining: A host-side hop connects to the VPS's static IPv4 and the VPS makes the upstream request, so the upstream sees an address in AS7018 (AT&T) or AS5650 instead of the caller's address.

limits.value: 2000 GB two-way traffic per month on the static VPS

limits_note: The vendor states the line is a real home broadband line laid locally with IP purity not guaranteed, that IPs are recycled, and that there is no free IP replacement. A shared dynamic NAT line (CNY 149 per month) is a separate product that, per the same review, needs real-name verification by phone number; the static line does not.
binding_note: 2000 GB a month is the only quota the vocabulary can express; stock is the practical limit, since both static lines showed sold out with a pre-order queue per a third-party review.

identity_cost.detail: The vendor writes '静态IP系列产品无需实名认证' (the static IP series needs no real-name verification). The WHMCS registration asks for a personal profile and a billing address and offers CNY or USD. The shared dynamic NAT line needs a real-name phone check, per a third-party review.

reliability_note: The vendor's page labels the second static line 'Verizon (AS5650)'; a RIPE Stat lookup returns FRONTIER-FRTR - Frontier Communications of America, Inc. as the holder of AS5650, so the Verizon label does not match the registry holder of that ASN. AS7018 resolves to ATT-INTERNET4 - AT&T Enterprises, LLC. No live exit address was looked up (rung 5).
confidence_note: The ASNs, the no-real-name statement and the specification are first-party; the price, stock and NAT-line identity come from a third-party review, which is the weakest rung used.

evidence.quote: 静态IP系列产品无需实名认证
evidence.proved: The static IP series needs no real-name verification.
The AT&T line is one dedicated static address under AS7018.
The second line is labelled Verizon with AS5650.

evidence.quote: 只保证IP是真家宽，不保证纯净度，无免费更换IP的政策
evidence.proved: The vendor guarantees only a real home broadband line, not purity, and has no free IP replacement.

evidence.quote: 前两条线目前都是 ¥149/月起，价格一致
evidence.proved: A third-party review reports CNY 149 per month from for the first two product lines.

evidence.quote: 需要手机号实名认证（官方注明作弊封号不退款）
evidence.proved: A third-party review reports the NAT line needs a phone-number real-name check.
RIPE Stat lists Frontier Communications as the holder of AS5650, not Verizon.
RIPE Stat lists AT&T Enterprises as the holder of AS7018.

notes: Named on a Chinese-language proxy forum as 'AaITR Frontier/Verizon 静态家宽 149元/月'. A VPS that carries one residential line, the same shape as the novixlink record.

extras.rung_note: The product is a claim about how an address is registered; two ASN holders were looked up, no live exit address.
